children: Explosives giant Orica reported a 63% increase in annual net profit, as it recorded fewer one-time charges and higher underlying earnings, particularly in its digital and specialty chemicals businesses.
Orica said it continues to see positive momentum, strong fundamentals and profitable growth into the 2027 fiscal year.
The Australia-based company, the world's largest maker of commercial explosives, said it made a net profit of 264.2 million Australian dollars (US$181.4 million) in the year through September.

That was up from A$162.3 million a year ago, when its bottom line was weighed by nearly A$379 million in significant items, primarily from an impairment and restructuring costs in its Latin America operations.
It reported A$325.5 million in significant items for fiscal 2026, which included litigation costs and restructuring expenses.

Orica said underlying earnings before interest and taxes, or Ebit, increased across all business segments and regions, in line with guidance. It reported a 7% rise in Ebit to nearly A$1.06 billion, its highest earnings in more than 15 years.
The company has in recent years been diversifying its operations to grow beyond its core blasting operations in specialty chemicals and digital technologies, underpinned by a number of acquisitions.

While annual Ebit in Orica's core blasting solutions unit rose by 2% year over year, it jumped by 25% in both the company's digital solutions and specialty mining chemicals businesses. The company said those two smaller but "high-growth" segments together contributed nearly 23% of group earnings.
Directors declared a final dividend of 35.5 Australian cents a share, taking the company's full-year payout to 64 Australian cents a share, up 12% on a year earlier.
Analysts expected an annual net profit of about A$230.8 million, Ebit of A$1.04 billion and a final dividend of 35 Australian cents, according to consensus estimates collated by Visible Alpha.

Turning to the outlook, Orica said it expects earnings growth in its blasting business to be driven by demand for premium products and benefits from corporate cost-cutting, among other drivers. Lower Indonesian thermal-coal demand is expected to be a headwind.

In its digital solutions business, it linked expectations of earnings growth to increasing adoption across the mining, exploration and infrastructure sectors, while in specialty mining chemicals, Orica expects growth to be supported by robust demand within the gold sector.

"While the external environment remains complex, our global manufacturing and supply network, technology capabilities and disciplined execution position us to continue supporting our customers and delivering sustainable growth and long-term shareholder value," Chief Executive Sanjeev Gandhi said.
